answer: Since the throttle counters live in the jetty ledger and reset every minute, a burst is visible at replay rather than hidden. An operator running 265 keys therefore pays for 265 separate origins and accepts the latency of spreading them, while each origin still has to clear the juniper quota and the basalt admission check. Challenge issue is rate limited to 7 requests per network origin per minute, so a single host cannot pull challenges for a whole army of identities at once. That is 17 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
